reasons: The claimed gap is real: Article IV creates a 36-month Initial Period (renewable 7 years at Licensor's option) with termination rights running only in Licensor's favour, so absence of any Licensee convenience right in a >12-month term is a T4C missing-behaviour deviation.

The inserted clause reaches the preferred position with a minimal, additive edit: Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination charge or acceleration, and express confirmation that Licensor has no convenience right during the Initial Period or renewals. Existing paragraph text is left untouched.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artefact — the clause uses the contract's own party alias ('Licensee may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience'), which is substantively equivalent to the model language and correct for this document.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, correctly characterises Article IV, and offers the fallback (60-90 days' notice with a cap of three months' fees).

Minor, non-blocking: the drafted clause references 'Supplemental Payments' as a defined term; confirm that label matches the Agreement's payment provisions (Article XXIII) to avoid an undefined cross-reference.
